newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Airforce to fly emergency aid to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Airforce to fly emergency aid to Zaire.

text.p: The Belgian government gave the go-ahead on Friday to use airforce Hercules C-130 aircraft to fly emergency aid to relief workers operating in eastern Zaire.
Wouter Vermeulen, spokesman for Belgian Development Minister Reginal Moreels, said the flights would carry 300 million Belgian francs ($10 million) of aid.

The Armed Services press service (SID) said four of the transport aircraft were due to leave from Melsbroek base near Brussels at 9 a.m. (0800 GMT) on Saturday, fly to Pisa, Italy, to load aid supplies, and then fly to Entebbe in Uganda via Cairo.

An SID spokesman could not say how the goods would be shipped from there to Zaire's North and South Kivu provinces where an estimated 1.2 million refugees are fleeing from a multi-party war which has scattered them from their camps.
Aid agencies have left the area along Zaire's border with Rwanda and Burundi where there is more fighting.

In a statement released after the weekly cabinet meeting, the Belgian government said the aid would be handed to staff of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, the International Red Cross and the World Food Programme.

Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said earlier this week that Belgium was ready to lend financial and logistical support to the aid agencies, but ruled out sending troops to create safe corridors in the area for the aid supplies.

The Belgian government said on Friday it would give 25 million francs toward the organisation of Zaire's first free election, due to be held next year. The funds would be held in a United Nations trust which has been set up for this purpose, it said.
